newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning,consolidate gains.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks slip in morning,consolidate gains.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks drifted lower in Thursday morning trade, with investors choosing to take a more cautious approach after the Hang Seng index hit a new year high this week.

"I think the market is starting to show some caution at this stage. Since the market has rallied quite a lot, people might just want to wait for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities (HK) Ltd.
The Hang Seng index was down 26.66 points at 11,567.37. Turnover was HK$1.11 billion after the first fifty minutes of trade.
The U.S. Federal Reserve policy-setting body meets on September 24.
Tsang said the Hang Seng could trade between 11,400 and 11,600 points until the meeting. The blue chip index hit a new intra-day year high at 11,645.35 on Tuesday.
"There is not much incentive to be in this market at this level," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"We are seeing some normal profit-taking and caution ahead of the FOMC," he said.
Mak said investors were also taking their cue from an overnight decline on Wall Street. The Dow industrials fell 11.47 points to 5,877.36 on Wednesday.
Analysts said the local market could make further headway once the FOMC meeting was behind it. "If there is no hike in rates then the market will move higher," said Mak.
Tsang said recent all-time highs in some blue chip stocks showed that underlying market sentiment was bullish. "We'll see some action after the FOMC," he added.
Among the few advancing blue chips on Thursday, Amoy Properties rose HK$0.10 to HK$9.20. The company is due to report earnings for the year ended June 30 on Friday.
Wheelock rose HK$0.25 to HK$16.85 and Bank of East Asia added HK$0.10 to HK$28.35.
Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.00 to HK$78.00 and Cheung Kong slipped HK$0.50 to HK$56.75.

Trading in China United shares resumed on Thursday. The stock rose HK$0.015 to HK$0.445 after the company said it had agreed to issue 72.87 million new shares at HK$0.433 per share to fund the purchase of an additional stake in a subsidiary.
Trading in Best Wide Group shares was suspended at the company's request pending an announcement. The stock closed at HK$0.56 on Wednesday.
